A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAGE research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and supplementary additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-explanation experiments, including validity, class probabilities, qualitative examples, timing measurements, and motif-threshold sensitivity.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds loss ablations, instance-level explainer comparisons, motif-extraction timings, and generated-graph novelty results.

M1.justification: The motif extraction, attention-based class-specific selection, junction-tree generation, and reconstruction/property objectives remain unchanged. Section 3.3.7 and Appendix A document sampling and graph assembly more explicitly without establishing an altered method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Mutagenicity, PTC_MR, PTC_MM, PTC_FM, AIDS, and NCI-H23. The added analyses reuse these molecular classification settings without introducing new datasets, populations, domains, or input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens comparator scope by adding instance-level GNNExplainer and GEM evaluations on Mutagenicity in Appendix G, Table 8. v1 evaluates XGNN, GNNInterpreter, and the motif-selection variant; these comparisons remain in v2.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols measure generated-graph novelty against the training set, average instance-level explainers' probabilities, and test separate loss components. The existing target-GCN setup and 1000-explanations-per-class probability evaluation remain unchanged. Newly disclosed explainer hyperparameter ranges do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds reconstruction-only and property-only ablations in Section 4.4, a memorization check through novelty in Appendix H, and motif-extraction efficiency analysis in Appendix D. These substantially extend the retained attention-selection ablation and threshold sensitivity study. The molecular examples are redistributed existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean class probabilities and standard deviations across 1000 generated explanations per class. Added probability tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting convention; no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds loss-component results, GNNExplainer probabilities of 0.8339/0.8250 and GEM probabilities of 0.8739/0.8887 for the two Mutagenicity classes, 100% novelty for both classes across all six datasets, and extraction times of 0.415–0.877 ms/graph. Main Tables 1–2 and the previous timing and threshold results are numerically unchanged. Section 4.2 corrects the win count from six of eight to ten of twelve and removes the 1.21% and 2.11% improvement statements.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the bond-feature matrix dimensions from N-by-Db to |E|-by-Db, indexing bonds by edges rather than atoms. This is a limited correction to a formal definition. No theorems or proofs are added, and the main objectives and derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about motif-based, class-specific, chemically valid and interpretable model-level explanations. The new contribution list restates these existing claims rather than introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the complementary loss components, attributes the instance-level comparison to advantages of global context, and interprets novelty as evidence against memorization. Appendix D also argues that motif extraction has negligible computational cost. Existing validity and motif-selection explanations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility documentation with decoder assembly and feasibility-filtering pseudocode, an explicit sampling description, and explainer epoch, learning-rate, and batch-size candidates. It identifies implementations for the new comparators and states how qualitative samples were selected. An explicit repository link replaces v1's supplemental-code disclosure; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Funke et al. on hard masking and Lin et al. on GEM, and extends its positioning against instance-level explainers. Section 3.3 recasts the generator discussion from tree-constrained/non-constrained to VAE/RL-based methods. The principal related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a contribution list and sampling explanation, clarifies terminology and loss names, and reorganizes the appendices while removing the NeurIPS checklist. Most existing scientific prose and the main section sequence are retained, so this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4, Algorithm 1, three numbered experimental tables, and an unnumbered extraction-time table. It enlarges existing figures and expands Table 3 using molecular examples moved from the appendices. Conference styling, captions, and display placement also change substantially; the expanded qualitative display does not represent newly generated examples.

improvement.justification: The added loss ablation and novelty check strengthen support for existing design choices, while decoder, sampling, and training details improve reproducibility. Correcting the win-count summary also improves reporting accuracy. These are useful incremental gains over unchanged main benchmark evidence. Appendix G's broader generalizability interpretation exceeds what its class-probability comparison alone establishes, limiting the strength of that addition.
